[Series](index.qmd) · [0 Foundations](foundations.qmd) · [1 Violin](violin.qmd) · [2 Clarinet](clarinet.qmd) · [3 Kalimba](kalimba.qmd) · **4 Piano** · [5 Drum](drum.qmd)

A piano string is a violin string that is also a little bit of a kalimba tine. The two restoring forces add, and the overtones creep sharp.

## Play it

```{=html}

.kbd .b { position: absolute; top: 0; height: 60%; background: var(--ink); border: 1px solid var(--ink); border-radius: 0 0 4px 4px; z-index: 2; padding: 0; min-height: 0; }
```

```{=html}
<div class="ins">

  <div class="slider" style="padding:0.75rem 0.25rem 0"><label for="mult">Stiffness ×</label><input type="range" id="mult" min="0" max="12" step="0.5" value="1"><output id="multo">1.0</output></div>
```

## Deriving the operator

A piano wire is under heavy tension, like a violin string, and it is thick steel, so it also resists bending, like a kalimba tine. Forces per unit length simply add: the tension term from [Part 0](foundations.qmd) and the bending term from [Part 3](kalimba.qmd) give
$$
\mu\,u_{tt} = T\,u_{xx} - EI\,u_{xxxx}, \qquad\text{that is}\qquad \mathcal{L} = -c^2\partial_x^2 + \kappa^2\partial_x^4 .
$$

Treat the ends as pinned: they cannot move and transmit no bending moment, so $u = u_{xx} = 0$. Real piano strings are held closer to clamped, which shifts the numbers slightly but not the picture.

## Spectrum

Pinned ends make $\sin(n\pi x/L)$ an eigenfunction of both terms at once. Substituting it gives $\omega^2 = c^2k^2 + \kappa^2 k^4$ with $k = n\pi/L$, so
$$
f_n = n f_0\sqrt{1 + Bn^2}, \qquad B = \frac{\pi^2 EI}{T L^2}.
$$

The stiffness constant $B$ is small, but it multiplies $n^2$, so high partials run noticeably sharp. Since $I$ grows like the fourth power of the wire's diameter and $B$ falls like $1/L^2$, short thick treble strings are the stiffest.

```{=html}
<div class="ins">
<div class="panel">
    <h3>Partials of the last key</h3>
    <svg class="spec" id="pSpec" viewBox="0 0 320 120" aria-label="Partials of the last key played"></svg>
    <div class="readout" id="pPart"></div>
    <p class="cap">Hammer at 1/8 of the length, so the 8th and 16th partials nearly vanish.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Why tuners stretch octaves

A tuner sets an octave by listening for beats between the lower note's second partial and the upper note's fundamental. Stiffness pushes that second partial above $2f_0$, so a beat-free octave is slightly wider than 2 : 1. Repeated across the keyboard, this is *stretch tuning*: the top of a piano is tuned sharp of equal temperament, and the bottom flat.

```{=html}
<div class="ins">
<div class="panel">
    <div class="controls"><button id="o21">C4 + C5, exactly 2 : 1</button><button id="ost" class="primary">C4 + C5, stretched</button></div>
    <div class="readout" id="oRead"></div>
    <p class="cap">Listen for the slow wobble in the 2 : 1 version. Raise the stiffness above to speed it up.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<script src="core.js"></script>
<script>
(function () {
  "use strict";
  var C = Core, mult = 1, cache = {}, last = 60;
  var KEYS = []; for (var k = 48; k <= 72; k++) KEYS.push(k);
  var BLACK = { 1: 1, 3: 1, 6: 1, 8: 1, 10: 1 };
  var kbd = document.getElementById("kbd"), whites = KEYS.filter(function (k) { return !BLACK[k % 12]; }), btn = {};
  whites.forEach(function (k) {
    var b = document.createElement("button"); b.type = "button"; b.className = "w"; b.dataset.key = k;
    b.textContent = k % 12 === 0 ? C.noteName(C.mtof(k)).name : ""; b.setAttribute("aria-label", C.noteName(C.mtof(k)).name);
    kbd.appendChild(b); btn[k] = b;
  });
  KEYS.forEach(function (k) {
    if (!BLACK[k % 12]) return;
    var wi = whites.indexOf(k - 1), b = document.createElement("button"); b.type = "button"; b.className = "b"; b.dataset.key = k;
    b.setAttribute("aria-label", C.noteName(C.mtof(k)).name);
    b.style.left = "calc(" + ((wi + 1) / whites.length * 100) + "% - " + (0.3 / whites.length * 100) + "%)"; b.style.width = (0.6 / whites.length * 100) + "%";
    kbd.appendChild(b); btn[k] = b;
  });
  function partsFor(k, f1, m) { return C.models.piano.partials({ B: C.models.piano.B(k, m == null ? mult : m), f1: f1 || C.mtof(k) }); }
  function buf(k) {
    var id = k + ":" + mult;
    if (!cache[id]) { var f = C.mtof(k); cache[id] = C.render(C.toHz(partsFor(k), f), Math.min(5, 1.5 + 3 * Math.pow(262 / f, 0.6))); }
    return cache[id];
  }
  function strike(k) {
    C.play(buf(k), 0.7); last = k; flash(k); pspec();
    var B = C.models.piano.B(k, mult), nn = C.noteName(C.mtof(k));
    document.getElementById("pRead").innerHTML = "<b>" + nn.name + "</b> · " + C.mtof(k).toFixed(1) + " Hz · B = <b>" + B.toExponential(1) + "</b>";
  }
  function flash(k) { var b = btn[k]; if (!b) return; b.classList.add("on"); setTimeout(function () { b.classList.remove("on"); }, 180); }
  var down = false, lastK = -1;
  function keyAt(e) { var el = document.elementFromPoint(e.clientX, e.clientY); return el && el.dataset && el.dataset.key ? parseInt(el.dataset.key, 10) : -1; }
  kbd.addEventListener("pointerdown", function (e) { e.preventDefault(); down = true; kbd.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId); var k = keyAt(e); lastK = k; if (k > 0) strike(k); });
  kbd.addEventListener("pointermove", function (e) { if (!down) return; var k = keyAt(e); if (k > 0 && k !== lastK) strike(k); lastK = k; });
  function up() { down = false; lastK = -1; }
  kbd.addEventListener("pointerup", up); kbd.addEventListener("pointercancel", up);
  kbd.addEventListener("click", function (e) { if (e.detail === 0 && e.target.dataset.key) strike(parseInt(e.target.dataset.key, 10)); });
  var MAP = { a: 60, w: 61, s: 62, e: 63, d: 64, f: 65, t: 66, g: 67, y: 68, h: 69, u: 70, j: 71, k: 72 };
  window.addEventListener("keydown", function (e) { if (e.repeat || e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey || e.target.tagName === "INPUT") return; var k = MAP[e.key.toLowerCase()]; if (k) strike(k); });

  var ms = document.getElementById("mult"), mo = document.getElementById("multo");
  ms.addEventListener("input", function () { mult = parseFloat(ms.value); mo.textContent = mult.toFixed(1); pspec(); octRead(); });

  function pspec() {
    var p = partsFor(last);
    C.stems(document.getElementById("pSpec"), p, { W: 320, H: 120, rmax: 16, fs: 8, sw: 2, labelEvery: 2 });
    var r10 = p[9] ? p[9].ratio : null;
    document.getElementById("pPart").innerHTML = C.noteName(C.mtof(last)).name + " · partial 2 at <b>" + (1200 * Math.log2(p[1].ratio / 2)).toFixed(1) + "¢</b> sharp" + (r10 ? " · partial 10 at <b>" + (1200 * Math.log2(r10 / 10)).toFixed(0) + "¢</b> sharp" : "");
  }
  function r2(k) { var B = C.models.piano.B(k, mult); return 2 * Math.sqrt((1 + 4 * B) / (1 + B)); }
  function octRead() {
    var f = C.mtof(60), beat = f * (r2(60) - 2);
    document.getElementById("oRead").innerHTML = "2 : 1 octave beats at <b>" + beat.toFixed(2) + " Hz</b> · stretched octave is <b>" + (1200 * Math.log2(r2(60) / 2)).toFixed(1) + "¢</b> wide";
  }
  function octave(stretch) {
    var f = C.mtof(60), f5 = stretch ? f * r2(60) : 2 * f;
    var a = C.toHz(partsFor(60, f), f), b = C.toHz(partsFor(72, f5), f5);
    b.forEach(function (p) { p.amp *= 0.8; });
    C.play(C.render(a.concat(b), 4.5), 0.8); flash(60); flash(72);
  }
  document.getElementById("o21").addEventListener("click", function () { octave(false); });
  document.getElementById("ost").addEventListener("click", function () { octave(true); });
  C.onTheme(pspec);
  pspec(); octRead();
})();
</script>
```
